title: Gemini won't clean up my Google Drive, so I let Claude do it; I'm not going back
content_html:
Published Sep 17, 2026, 6:00 AM EDT

I’ve been covering Android since 2023, when I joined Android Police, mostly focusing on AI and everything around Pixel and Galaxy phones. I’ve got a bachelor’s in IT with a major in AI, so I naturally view technology differently. I usually take a pro-consumer angle instead of the marketing hype, which you’ve probably noticed in my writing.

My Google Drive root folder is, to put it kindly, a digital landfill.

It's full of PDFs I don't remember downloading, screenshots called things like Screenshot 2024-03-11 at 9.42.17 am, and the same file duplicated across half a dozen folders.

I have a digital hygiene routine. But life has been chaotic lately, and living in the age of AI has made me lazier than I'd like to admit.

And speaking of AI, isn't this the sort of mind-numbing admin AI was meant to absorb to keep the day from unraveling?

Gemini is happy to tell me what's wrong with my Google Drive, but it stops there. It doesn't act on what it finds, which is what I always wanted.

That's what sent me looking for an alternative, and that's how I found what I wanted in Claude.

Gemini can see the mess but won't touch it

Google built the hands, then tied them

Gemini is good at research; I'll give it that. Point Gemini at a dense PDF or ask it to dig up an email from three months ago, and it handles both without complaint.

But you can't tell Gemini to clean up your root directory. You can't ask it to move old project assets into a folder or trash outdated drafts.

Gemini's chat integration with Drive is read-only by design. It can search and summarize, but there's no move, rename, or trash.

Google tried this. For nine months, Gemini's Drive side panel could move files by natural-language command, five at a time.

But then it pulled the feature in April 2026, and what replaced it tells you where the company's head is at.

Claude got write access to my Drive in August

Say the job, get the job

Anthropic saw the same sandbox and decided to open the gate. In August 2026, it updated Claude's Google Workspace connectors, and just like that, Claude went from finding your files to doing things with them.

It can create folders, upload files to your Drive, and check recent changes. You describe the job in plain language, Claude interprets it, and does the job. Everything is as simple as that.

What Claude did with my 'Document (7).pdf' pile

Next time, it could run without me

My first go at it was an "Oh, it just did that" moment. As I said, my Drive root was a landfill, and the filenames were no help. Things like "Document (7).pdf" and "IMG_20260318_143212.png."

I asked Claude to read the contents and sort it into subfolders, and it nailed the job. It read closely enough to catch a mismatch between an invoice's filename date and the date printed inside it.

That was one afternoon of prompting, and it barely scratched the surface. Anyone handy with coding could turn that cleanup into a recurring task, so it never builds up again.

Nothing moves until I click confirm

Approvals are on by default, for good reason

I find the idea of handing a third-party model the power to trash my tax returns unnerving, since a hallucination could ruin my workflow and take out a file in about two seconds.

Anthropic built guardrails around that. By default, Claude asks for explicit approval before executing any move, share, or trash command.

That default is yours to change. If you'd rather Claude just get on with it, you can turn the confirmations off and let it run YOLO, though I'd want a backup first.

It shows you the proposed action in the chat and waits for you to click confirm, so nothing disappears in the background without you seeing it.

Your existing Workspace permissions also carry over. Claude can't touch anything you don't already have the right to control.

Organize My Files still makes you do the clicking

Safe, sensible, and slow

Google knows your Drive is a disaster, but it chose the supervised route. In June 2026, the company made a feature called Organize My Files.

It uses Gemini to suggest folder structures, but everything happens inside a dashboard. The Suggest file moves button in Drive, and Gemini analyzes your unsorted files and builds a cleanup plan.

From there it's you and a dashboard. You review each suggestion, uncheck anything you'd rather not touch, rename folders inline if the names don't suit, then sign off on the batch move.

It's safe, it works, but you'll still do the clicking. Me, I'd rather type a sentence and go put the kettle on.

Google chose caution, while Anthropic chose action

So here's the odd place we've ended up. If you want real agentic control over your Google Drive, you have to hand your data to Anthropic.

I don't think either company got this wrong, and I can follow the reasoning on both sides.

Google chose caution, keeping Gemini mostly in read mode, so your files stay intact.

Anthropic chose action, then handed you the responsibility of approving anything destructive. With a root folder like mine, Anthropic's path is the easy choice.
